content.user_title: Build htmx Interfaces with Local References
content.value_statement: htmx questions often need exact attribute, event, and header behavior. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a local htmx reference index.
actual_capabilities: Finds local pages for htmx attributes, events, headers, API methods, extensions, and examples.
Explains common htmx attributes such as hx-get, hx-post, hx-swap, hx-trigger, and hx-vals.
Points users to example pages for modals, tabs, bulk updates, progress bars, and forms.
Uses the local reference index to answer syntax and behavior questions.
Supports targeted searches across the references folder when the right page is unclear.
limitations: It depends on the included local documentation snapshot.
It does not run browser, server, or integration tests.
Documentation examples still need application security review before production use.
Regenerating references with the builder script requires network access.

use_cases.title: Implement htmx Attributes
use_cases.description: Look up exact attribute behavior before adding dynamic requests to server-rendered pages.

use_cases.title: Design Server Responses
use_cases.description: Find headers, events, and swap behavior needed for predictable htmx responses.

use_cases.title: Explain htmx Patterns
use_cases.description: Reference examples and API pages when writing clear guidance for teams.

prompt_templates.title: Find an Attribute
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the htmx reference page for hx-target and explain when to use it.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare hx-swap and hx-swap-oob for updating multiple page regions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an htmx modal form workflow using the local reference examples and headers.

prompt_templates.title: Review htmx Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my htmx approach for security, swap behavior, validation, and event handling.

output_examples.input: How should I load a modal with htmx?
output: Use the modal examples as the starting point.
Confirm the target element, swap strategy, and close behavior.
Validate server responses before reusing example markup.
Use static JSON values for simple request parameters.
Avoid evaluated values with user-controlled input.
Read the security notes before using dynamic JavaScript values.

output_examples.input: Where are htmx response headers documented?
output_examples.output: The skill points to the headers reference pages and explains each header purpose.

best_practices: Open the most specific reference page before answering detailed htmx questions.
Treat examples as starting points and validate all server-side behavior.
Check security notes for evaluated values, headers, and user-generated content.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every htmx request is safe without server validation.
Do not use evaluated attribute values with untrusted input.
Do not present CDN examples as the only installation method.

faq.question: What does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers htmx attributes, events, headers, API methods, extensions, examples, and related patterns.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: It includes documentation and examples, but it does not execute an application.

faq.question: Can it answer exact syntax questions?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses local reference files to answer syntax and behavior questions.

faq.question: Does it replace the official htmx site?
faq.answer: No. It is a local snapshot and may trail the newest official documentation.

faq.question: Is it useful for security review?
faq.answer: It can highlight documented security notes, but it does not perform full application testing.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
